turns.user_message: Storage grows 4% per month from 120 TB. When will we pass 200 TB? Show the calculation.

steps.reasoning: The user asks a calculation, not related to data. We can compute: starting at {{int:96:144}} TB, growth 4% per month compound. Find number of months n such that {{int:96:144}}*(1.04)^n > {{int:160:240}}. Solve: (1.04)^n > 200/120 = 1.6666667. Take ln: n > ln(1.6667)/ln(1.04). Compute approximate: ln(1.6667)=0.510826, ln(1.04)=0.039221. n > 13.02. So after {{int:11:17}} months it will exceed {{int:160:240}} TB. Show calculation. Provide answer.
steps.text:
**Calculation**

We need the smallest whole number of months *n* such that the storage exceeds {{int:160:240}} TB when it grows 4 % each month starting from {{int:96:144}} TB.

The growth is compounded monthly:

\[
\text{Storage after } n \text{ months} = {{int:96:144}} \times (1.04)^{n}
\]

Set this greater than {{int:160:240}} TB:

\[
{{int:96:144}} \times (1.04)^{n} > {{int:160:240}}
\]

\[
(1.04)^{n} > \frac{{{int:160:240}}}{{{int:96:144}}} = 1.666\overline{6}
\]

Take natural logarithms:

\[
n \times \ln(1.04) > \ln(1.666\overline{6})
\]

\[
n > \frac{\ln(1.666\overline{6})}{\ln(1.04)}
\]

Compute the values:

- \(\ln(1.666\overline{6}) \approx 0.5108\)
- \(\ln(1.04) \approx 0.03922\)

\[
n > \frac{0.5108}{0.03922} \approx 13.02
\]

Since *n* must be a whole month, we round up:

\[
\boxed{n = {{int:11:17}}\ \text{months}}
\]

**Result**

Starting from {{int:96:144}} TB and growing at 4 % per month, the storage will surpass {{int:160:240}} TB after **{{int:11:17}} months**. At that point the capacity will be:

\[
{{int:96:144}} \times (1.04)^{{{int:11:17}}} \approx {{int:96:144}} \times 1.749 \approx 209.9\ \text{TB}
\]
